name: Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia
aliases: Lymphoplasmacytic Lymphoma with IgM Monoclonal Gammopathy

ethnicAssociations: Rare in African and Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: 2nd International Workshop on Waldenstrom's Macroglobulinemia Consensus Criteria

criteria.description: IgM monoclonal gammopathy of any concentration
Bone marrow infiltration by small lymphocytes showing plasmacytoid or plasma cell differentiation (lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: IgM monoclonal protein plus bone marrow involvement by lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: MYD88 L265P mutation found in >90% of WM cases and helps distinguish from other IgM-secreting lymphomas. Not all patients with IgM MGUS progress to WM.

pathognomonic.notes: Visual disturbances, headache, bleeding, confusion due to elevated IgM causing blood viscosity increase

common.notes: Anti-MAG neuropathy; symmetric distal sensorimotor neuropathy

occasional.symptomName: Raynaud phenomenon and cold agglutinin disease

rare.notes: Direct CNS infiltration by lymphoplasmacytic cells
Chronic urticarial rash with IgM gammopathy

laboratory: IgM monoclonal protein on serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation
imaging: PET/CT may show mild FDG uptake (lower than aggressive lymphoma)
Fundoscopic exam showing dilated retinal veins, hemorrhages (hyperviscosity)
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing lymphoplasmacytic infiltration
Flow cytometry: CD19+, CD20+, CD22+, surface IgM+; CD5-, CD10-, CD23 variable
Serum viscosity measurement (normal <1.8 cP; symptomatic usually >4 cP)

distinguishingFeatures: IgM MGUS has no bone marrow infiltration
May secrete IgM but usually lower levels

redFlags: Symptomatic hyperviscosity (visual changes, confusion, bleeding) - medical emergency requiring plasmapheresis
Rapid rise in IgM level suggesting disease transformation
Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (Richter-like)
references: Owen RG, et al. Clinicopathological definition of Waldenstrom's macroglobulinemia: consensus panel recommendations from the Second International Workshop on Waldenstrom's Macroglobulinemia. Semin Oncol. 2003;30(2):110-115.
Kastritis E, et al. Waldenström's macroglobulinaemia: ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines. Ann Oncol. 2018;29(suppl 4):iv41-iv50.
Treon SP. How I treat Waldenström macroglobulinemia. Blood. 2015;126(6):721-732.
Gertz MA. Waldenström macroglobulinemia: 2021 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Am J Hematol. 2021;96(2):258-269.
